direction: ASSIGNED — the cold-storage specimen archive (grounded candidate 4 of 7)
prompt: A desktop website homepage design for 'ELUNE LABS', a research-peptide supplier, rendered as a full-bleed desktop browser viewport with NO browser chrome. A UI design — a screenshot of a shipped web page, NOT a poster, NOT a photograph with text on it. The organising world is the cold-storage cryogenic peptide archive: an addressable inventory of labelled specimens in racked cryoboxes, photographed and typeset with laboratory rigour. The archive is a coordinate and specification system for the catalog, not a depiction of a warehouse. Regions: slim header with ELUNE LABS wordmark and five category links; a ruled rack index band of twelve bordered cells R01-R12 with one filled to mark selection; a two-column hero, left a still-life photograph of one borosilicate vial in a cryobox cell, right a flat spec record panel of hairline-ruled label/value rows (LOT, CAS, FORMULA, MW, SEQUENCE, PURITY, FORM, STORAGE, QTY) with product name and price at its top edge; a full-width cryobox rack grid of square cells, each holding a vial glyph and a distinct compound name over a unique lot code, a few cells empty, three tagged LOW; a footer with the RUO line. Style: precise printed-laboratory rigour — flat fills, hairline cool-grey rules, square corners, condensed uppercase labels paired with a monospaced data face, strict grid, generous white space. No gradients, no neon, no glow, no blur, no dark mode, no black background, no people.
